contract.mutual_exclusion: At most one thread runs the ladder, the EXIT write, the reap and the pipe close of one range (single flight: the claim of a _Flight under an RLock that guards one pointer).
contract.idempotence: A call after a release has ended touches nothing and returns as before: None once reaped; a new ladder after RangeNotEmpty (mutation.py:1583 relies on it). A caller that WAITED for a release in flight is given its outcome: a copy of RangeNotEmpty/RangeEscaped (cause = the leader's), so a leak is never silent for it; a leader that died of something else produces no outcome and the waiter leads.
contract.ownership: _signal is reached only from _ladder; the anchor can be reaped only after flight.disposing is set; across threads the flight excludes a second signaller, on one thread a re-entry past the ladder returns without touching anything; the _reaped guard stays. A waiter never signals a range another thread emptied (BASE: ('SIGINT', True), 40/40).
contract.deadlock_freedom: Same thread re-entered: the claim lock is an RLock; a re-entry in the ladder runs the ladder, past it returns at once; it never waits for itself. Another thread: polls flight.done with time.sleep(POLL_S), holds nothing, waits exactly as long as the release (bounded by grace_s/wait_s; unbounded with wait_s=None, as its own ladder was). Abandoned StoryScope worker: a later caller waits for it and is free when it ends. start()->_abort() runs before the range is shared and overlaps nothing.

mechanism.chosen: single flight: _Flight{thread, disposing, escaped, done, outcome}; release() = claim under _mx (RLock) -> lead (_ladder, disposing=True, _release tail) | wait by polling and share the outcome | re-entry (ladder if not disposing, else return); outcome raised after the finally

mechanism.why: The contract needed an owner (re-entry), an outcome (the waiter) and a phase (ownership); a lock carries none of them. An RLock does guard the claim, because a handler may land inside it (test: a plain Lock there hangs).
